findings.issue: The cooperative contract forbids late ordinary commits and any cleanup commit at K, but its concrete SQLite strategy only qualifies cancellable lock acquisition plus busy/progress/interrupt hooks. It never defines or tests the race between the final context check and transaction COMMIT, or a cancellation/second stop that arrives after COMMIT has begun. rusqlite 0.39 Transaction::commit invokes a separate execute_batch("COMMIT"); busy/progress cancellation of earlier statements alone is not proof that this terminal operation respects the promised write fence. The independent expiry status and eventual join do not establish whether a write committed during that race.
findings.required_correction: Have c-1 freeze the commit-versus-stop linearization/outcome contract for both ordinary and restricted-cleanup transactions and qualify a supported SQLite commit guard/callback or equivalent mechanism on rusqlite0.39. C-5 needs causal tests pausing after the last ordinary check and at commit admission, racing G/K, deadline shortening and second stop, and verifying actual persisted state plus accurate error/outcome after physical join. Do not hold a cancellation-controller lock across potentially blocking COMMIT, replay uncertain mutations, or claim rollback/no-late-write solely from expiry notification. If the strict approved guarantee cannot be implemented with supported APIs, report that capability gap before freezing cooperative support rather than silently weakening the requirement.
